stem:
Ananya asks what integer $q$ satisfies $(-4) \times q = -36$.

Which claim is correct?

options.text: $q = -9$, because the product $(-4) \times q$ must be negative.
Division asks for $q$ in $q \div (-4) = -36$, so reverse the missing-factor layout.
$q = 144$, from writing $(-4) \times q$ as adding the absolute values.

teacher.key_rationale: (-4)×9 = -36, so q = 9 and (-36)÷(-4) = 9. The product is already negative with positive q. The missing factor multiplies by the divisor. Addition is not the operation.
